title: Stage set for 80th Independence Day Celebrations at Red Fort
subtitle:
Prime Minister to lead the grand celebrations commemorating ‘150 Years of Vande Mataram’ & ‘Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047’
‘Vande Mataram’ to be rendered for the first time as part of the celebrations
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will lead the 80 th Independence Day Celebrations from the Red Fort in Delhi on August 15, 2026. The grand event is set to commemorate 150 years of the enduring legacy of the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’ and celebrate the energy, aspirations and pivotal contribution of ‘Yuva Shakti’ in driving India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. For the first time, ‘Vande Mataram’ will be rendered during the celebrations at Red Fort.
The Ceremony
Upon his arrival at the Red Fort, the Prime Minister will be received by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth and Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh. The Defence Secretary will introduce the General Officer Commanding (GoC), Delhi Area Lieutenant General Rajesh Sethi to the Prime Minister. The GoC, Delhi Area will then conduct the Prime Minister to the Saluting Base where a combined Inter-Services and Delhi Police Guard will present general salute to Shri Narendra Modi. Thereafter, the Prime Minister will inspect the Guard of Honour.
The Guard of Honour contingent for the Prime Minister will consist of one officer & 24 personnel each from the Army, Navy, Air Force & Delhi Police. The Indian Army is the coordinating service for the Independence Day Celebrations this year. The Guard of Honour will be commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Arjun Singh. The Army contingent in the Prime Minister’s Guard will be commanded by Major Aditya Sharma, the Naval contingent by Lieutenant Commander Neelam Rana and the Air Force contingent by Squadron Leader Vipin Kumar. The Delhi Police contingent will be commanded by Additional DCP Shri Vineet Kumar.
After inspecting the Guard of Honour, the Prime Minister will proceed to the ramparts of the Red Fort where he will be greeted by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh, Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan and Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth. The GoC, Delhi area will conduct the Prime Minister to the dais on the ramparts to hoist the National Flag.
Captain Sonia Singh Chauhan will assist the Prime Minister in hoisting the National Flag. It will be synchronised with the 21-Gun Salute by the valiant gunners of the 1721 Field Battery (Ceremonial). The ceremonial battery, utilising the indigenous 105mm Light Field Guns, will be commanded by Major Pawan Singh Shekhawat and the Gun Position Officer will be Naib Subedar (Assistant Instructor in Gunnery) Anuthosh Sarkar.
The National Flag Guard, comprising one officer and 32 Other Ranks each from the Army, Navy & Air Force and Delhi Police, will present the Rashtriya Salute at the time of hoisting of the National Flag by the Prime Minister. Major Lokendra Singh Shekhawat will be in command of this Inter-Services Guard and Police Guard.
The Army Contingent in the National Flag Guard will be commanded by Major Vikas Yadav, the Naval contingent by Lieutenant Commander Abhilash and the Air Force Contingent by Squadron Leader Umesh G. The Delhi Police contingent will be commanded by Additional DCP Shri Vikas Meena.
After being hoisted, the Tricolour will receive a ‘Rashtriya Salute’. The Army band, consisting of one JCO and 25 Other Ranks, will play the tune of ‘Vande Mataram’ and the national song will be sung by everyone present at Red Fort. It will be followed by the recitation of the National Anthem. The Band will be conducted by Subedar Ishwar Singh.
As soon as the National Flag is hoisted by the Prime Minister, flower petals will be showered at the venue by two Mi-17 helicopters of the Indian Air Force - one trooping the national flag and the other trooping a flag depicting ‘Vande Mataram’. The captains of the helicopters will be Wing Commander Rajat and Squadron Leader Ankit Varshney.
After the showering of flower petals, the Prime Minister will address the Nation. At the conclusion of his speech, the cadets of National Cadet Corps (NCC) and ‘My Bharat’ volunteers will sing the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’ followed by the National Anthem. A total of 2,500 boy & girl cadets (Army, Navy and Air Force) and ‘My Bharat’ volunteers will participate in the celebrations. These cadets & ‘My Bharat’ volunteers will be seated on Gyanpath, opposite the Rampart. They will be forming ‘वंदे मातरम्’. View cutters depicting the theme ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’ will be installed at Gyanpath.
Special Guests
Approx. 5,000 Special Guests, from different walks of life, have been invited to witness the celebrations at Red Fort this year. These include:
International Yoga Day Volunteers Women Entrepreneurs under PM Mudra Yojana Beneficiaries under NAMASTE, PM AJAY, SEED Best performing MY Bharat Volunteers Best performing beneficiaries of PMAY(U) Street vendors under PM SVANidhi Urban sanitation workers under Swachh Bharat Mission Best performing Delhi Metro workers Best performing workers of Kartavya Path/Central Vista Youth innovators under National Innovation Programmes Best Innovators/Scientists in different fields Sarthi/Cab Driver/Taxi Drivers of Bharat Taxi in Delhi Best interns under Prime Minister Internship Scheme Best performing start-ups supported under various schemes Best performing Youth trained under PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana Best performing start-ups supported under Start-up India Seed Fund Nursing Orderlies (Ward Attendants) and other staff of Government Hospitals in Delhi PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana beneficiaries Artisans under PM Vishwakarma scheme Best performing beneficiaries under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Yojana Best performing farmers under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) Best performing students of various quizzes, competitions etc of Delhi government schools
Over 1,500 people from various States/Union Territories dressed in traditional attire have also been invited to witness the grand ceremony.
Public Convenience
Provision of cloak room : The availability of cloak rooms was applauded by visitors during Republic Day Celebrations. For the ease of users, 25 cloak rooms at six locations have been installed for the forthcoming Independence Day Celebrations. Volunteers at helpdesk : 200 volunteers - 100 from NCC & 100 from ‘MY Bharat’ - will assist visitors along with police personnel in reaching the enclosures. The volunteers can be identified on the way to the Red Fort. Provision of Wheelchairs : NCC cadets will be present at metro stations and parking areas for all the visitors who need assistance with wheelchairs. Metro Services : Metro will be operational from 4 AM on 15 th August for people to reach the venue. The Metro Services will be provided free of cost to all invitees. Metro QR codes are being provided with e-invitation. Parking facility at Parade Ground : Parking facility will be available for visitors with valid parking/labels. Ramp facility for pedestrians : To facilitate smooth movement of pedestrians from upper Subhash Marg to lower Subhash Marg, more robust ramps and stairs have been installed. Use of Google & Mappls Maps : On the day of the main event, traffic restrictions will be available on Google & Mappls Maps to facilitate the citizens. Invitation Card : This year, the invitation card depicts the Seva Teerth & Dharam Chakra. Rain Ponchos : Owing to the unpredictable weather conditions on the day of the main ceremony, rain ponchos will be provided to all invitees in Madhav Das Park and August 15 Park in addition to the dignitaries at the Rampart.
Names of Enclosures
To end VIP culture and underscore the importance of water conservation, the seating enclosures were named after rivers in Republic Day 2026. For the Independence Day Celebrations, the names of the seating enclosures have been named after major lakes of India. These include Badkhal, Bhimtal, Chandratal, Chilika, Dalpat Sagar, Dimna, Dudhsagar, Haflong, Harike, Hussain Sagar, Kanwar, Kankaria, Kolleru, Loktak, Lonar, Pangong Tso, Pulicat, Pushkar, Rabindra Sarobar, Ramgarh Tal, Rudrasagar, Sakhya Sagar, Shanti Sagar, Vembanad and Wular.
Swachhata Campaign
This year, a post-event Swachhata Campaign is being organised at Red Fort involving NCC cadets and MY Bharat Volunteer. The objective of the campaign is to ensure systematic plogging and prompt removal of garbage after dispersal of spectators right after the ceremony at Red Fort.
Drainage Management
In view of potential rainfall during the Independence Day Ceremony, several measures have been taken to prevent water overflow. Drainage and sewage systems in-and-around the Red Fort and nearby premises are being thoroughly cleaned.
Competitions
In the run up to Independence Day, quizzes and competitions were conducted by Ministry of Defence in collaboration with My Gov. The details of the competitions are as follows:
Essay Competition on ‘Role of AI in building a Viksit Bharat by 2047’ Painting Competition on ‘India 1947 vs India 2047’ Online quiz contests on ‘Constitution of India – Fundamental rights, duties, key articles and makers’; Women in India’s Freedom Movement – From Rani Lakshmibai to Sarojini Naidu and beyond; Major milestones of Modern India : Technological progresses and achievement in Space Technology; and India's success story in Nuclear Technology
Around 600 winners of the competitions will also be part of the celebrations. Other Ministries/Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi and Delhi Police also organised the following online quizzes and activities:
Education Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi : My Bharat Collage Competition; Salute the Heroes – Wall Display Activity; Cultural Fusion Performances/Competitions; Quiz Relay; Recycled Tricolor Art Activity; Tiranga Cyclothon; Tiranga Run; Tiranga Walkathon; Har Ghar Tiranga Delhi Police : Debate competition on True Patriotism; Patriotic song singing competition; Essay writing and quiz competition on freedom Fighters; Slogan writing and creative writing competition on National Integrity; Poster making and painting competition on ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’; Street play on National Unity; Awareness programmes against drug abuse; Women's safety and self-defence programme; Cyber awareness and cyber security programme; and 'Unity in Diversity' cultural programme.
Band Performances
To promote patriotic fervor among citizens and celebrate Independence Day, a number of band performances are being held at 343 prominent locations across the country. The performances are being carried out by the bands of Army, Navy, Air Force, Indian Coast Guard, NCC, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Border Security Force (BSF), Integrated Defence Staff (IDS), Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Assam Rifles. Entry to these band performance venues is open to the public.
Flag Hoisting on islands
Flag hoisting will be carried out by the Indian Navy and local administration in Andaman & Nicobar Island and Lakshadweep.

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead India's 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on 15 August 2026, themed around '150 Years of Vande Mataram' and 'Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047'. For the first time, 'Vande Mataram' will be formally rendered as part of the ceremony, alongside the traditional flag hoisting, 21-Gun Salute, Guard of Honour, and an address to the nation. The event will host around 5,000 special guests drawn from various government schemes and 2,500 NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers, with seating enclosures this year named after major Indian lakes.
enrichment.context:
Independence Day at the Red Fort is India's most significant annual constitutional and ceremonial event, commemorating the transfer of power from British rule on 15 August 1947. This year's 80th anniversary celebration is symbolically tied to the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram', composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in 1876 (published in Anandamath in 1882), which served as a rallying cry during the freedom movement and was adopted as the National Song by the Constituent Assembly in 1950, distinct from the National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'. The pairing of this historical theme with 'Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047' reflects the government's continuing push to link India's demographic dividend with its goal of becoming a developed nation by the 100th year of independence (2047), a vision articulated since 2022's 'Amrit Kaal' framing.

The event also serves as a showcase for a wide array of flagship government schemes—PM Mudra Yojana, PM SVANidhi, PM-KVY, Start-up India, PM Surya Ghar, PM Vishwakarma, PM-JAY-linked PM AJAY, and others—by inviting their beneficiaries as special guests, a practice that has become a hallmark of recent Republic Day and Independence Day celebrations to project inclusive governance. The naming of enclosures after lakes (following the 2026 Republic Day practice of naming them after rivers) continues a symbolic push for water conservation awareness and de-emphasizing VIP culture, consistent with the Jal Shakti Abhiyan and Catch the Rain campaigns.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to 'Vande Mataram', consider the following statements:
1. It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
2. It was adopted as the National Anthem of India by the Constituent Assembly.
3. It originally appeared in the novel 'Anandamath'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee and first appeared in his novel 'Anandamath'. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly as the National Song (not National Anthem) in 1950, giving it equal status of respect with the National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'.

prelims_questions.question: As per the release on the 80th Independence Day celebrations at Red Fort in 2026, the theme 'Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat' is linked to India's goal of becoming a developed nation by which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: The government has set 2047, the 100th year of India's independence, as the target year for achieving the vision of 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India).

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of 'Vande Mataram' in India's freedom struggle and examine its constitutional status as the National Song vis-à-vis the National Anthem.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 1 - Indian History: Freedom Struggle and National Symbols

mains_questions.question: The Independence Day celebrations increasingly showcase beneficiaries of various government welfare schemes as 'special guests'. Critically examine how such symbolic gestures contribute to the larger narrative of inclusive governance and 'Viksit Bharat@2047'.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance: Government Policies and Interventions
